observations: Photo 0: a bare used car engine sitting on a dirty floor in what looks like a parts market, with other engines and a gearbox around it.
It looks like a V-type petrol engine with the intake and throttle body on top, belts, pulleys and alternator at the front, wiring harness still attached.
No brand badge, engine code or plate is readable on the engine in photo 0.
Photo 0 carries a dealer watermark 'VICTOR MAZECO' and 'posted on Jiji'; the bottom bar is a phone camera stamp, not the item.
The engine is dusty and greasy, consistent with a used imported (tokunbo) engine, not a new one.
No gearbox match, mileage, running clip or compression evidence is shown.

read_from: photo 0: engine visible, no badge or engine code readable

claims.evidence: No Lexus or Toyota badge and no engine code (the LX460 uses a 1UR-FE) is readable in photo 0; identity rests on the seller's text alone.
The engine looks used and imported, but nothing in photo 0 shows its origin.
Photo 0 shows a dirty, dusty used engine on a workshop floor.
Internal history cannot be seen in a photo; unbroken factory seals on the heads and sump would only partly support it.
No running clip, no compression test, no clip of it fitted in a car.
No receipt or warranty document is shown.

risks.risk: The engine is not the claimed LX460 unit (a different, cheaper engine of similar look).
risks.proof: A clear close-up of the engine code stamped on the block and the plate or label on the engine.
risks.if_unproven: Cannot be priced; the engine code sets the price.

risks.risk: Engine does not run or has low compression, knocking or a cracked block.
risks.proof: A video of the engine running on a test stand or in a car from cold start, plus a compression test reading.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as not working, a core for rebuild.

risks.risk: Missing or damaged ancillaries (ECU, alternator, starter, harness).
risks.proof: A walkaround clip of all sides of the engine showing each ancillary included.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as a long block without ancillaries.

risks.risk: Internal damage or a previous rebuild hidden inside.
risks.proof: Photos of the oil filler cap underside and dipstick oil, and of the sump and head seals.

proof_requests: A sharp close-up of the engine code stamped on the block, readable in full.
A cold-start running video of this exact engine with the seller's handwritten code and date in shot.
A walkaround clip of all four sides showing the ancillaries included.
A photo of the oil under the filler cap and on the dipstick.
The receipt and warranty document, if they exist.
response.reason: Photo 0 shows a used V-type engine but nothing readable says which engine it is, and an engine's price is set by its code, so not even a worst case price is possible until the engine code is shown.
